name: Construction grid
summary: Letters and marks drawn on a fixed grid of squares and circles, so that each glyph in a set has the same size, weight and corner.
how: Fix one live area inside a square canvas; on a 24 unit canvas, keep a 2 unit margin.
Define 4 keyline shapes (circle, square, tall and wide rectangle) and fit each glyph to the one that suits it.
Cut every angle to 45° or 90°, or to one other fixed angle.
Use one stroke weight for the full set, for example 2 units on a 24 unit canvas.

origin.note: Albrecht Duerer publishes letters built with ruler and compass on a square grid in Underweysung der Messung.

adoptions.via: The committee of the Academie des Sciences draws the Romain du roi on a grid of 2304 small squares.
Herbert Bayer draws the Universal alphabet at the Bauhaus with a compass and a ruler.
Paul Renner draws Futura from the circle, the square and the triangle.
Otl Aicher builds the pictograms of the Munich Olympics on a grid with angles of 45° and 90° only.
The Twitter bird is drawn from overlapping circles with set radii.
Material Design sets 24 dp icons with a 20 dp live area and keyline shapes.

sources.title: Google, Material Design system icons guidelines (2014)
